top_signals.title: Standard Chartered: Oil Needs a New Shock to Fall Further
top_signals.summary: Oil prices continued to recover from their recent slump, with renewed Middle East supply threats outweighing earlier global surplus concerns. Brent crude for January delivery climbed 1.3% to trade at $95.90 per barrel at 12.00 pm ET on Thursday, a sharp rise after closing at $89.37/bbl on Monday while the corresponding WTI crude contract was up 1.2% to change hands at $84.65/ bbl. Yemen's Houthi forces claimed on Wednesday that their strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and export complex caused fires, with satellite imagery from NASA…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.
